passages.text: Better a dry morsel in quietness than a house full of feasting with strife.
passages.sermon:
A dry piece of bread is better than a feast with fighting.
Peace is more valuable than abundance with conflict.
Quietness brings more good than a house filled with arguments.
It is better to have little and live in peace than to have much and live with strife.
passages.original: ט֤וֹב פַּ֣ת חֲ֭רֵבָה וְשַׁלְוָה־ בָ֑הּ מִ֝בַּ֗יִת מָלֵ֥א זִבְחֵי־ רִֽיב׃

passages.text: A wise servant will rule over a disgraceful son and share his inheritance as one of the brothers.
passages.sermon:
A wise servant acts with understanding.
A wise servant will rule over a son who brings shame.
A wise servant will share in the inheritance among the brothers.
A disgraceful son loses his place of honor.
The wise servant gains authority and a share in the family inheritance.
passages.original: עֶֽבֶד־ מַשְׂכִּ֗יל יִ֭מְשֹׁל בְּבֵ֣ן מֵבִ֑ישׁ וּבְת֥וֹךְ אַ֝חִ֗ים יַחֲלֹ֥ק נַחֲלָֽה׃

passages.text: A crucible for silver and a furnace for gold, but the LORD is the tester of hearts.
passages.sermon:
A crucible tests silver.
A furnace tests gold.
The LORD tests hearts.
The LORD examines what is inside each person.
The LORD knows every thought and motive.
passages.original: מַצְרֵ֣ף לַ֭כֶּסֶף וְכ֣וּר לַזָּהָ֑ב וּבֹחֵ֖ן לִבּ֣וֹת יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: A wicked man listens to evil lips; a liar gives ear to a destructive tongue.
passages.sermon: A wicked man listens to evil lips.\r\nA liar listens to a destructive tongue.
passages.original: מֵ֭רַע מַקְשִׁ֣יב עַל־ שְׂפַת־ אָ֑וֶן שֶׁ֥קֶר מֵ֝זִין עַל־ לְשׁ֥וֹן הַוֺּֽת׃

passages.text: He who mocks the poor insults their Maker; whoever gloats over calamity will not go unpunished.
passages.sermon:
A person mocks the poor.
This person insults the Maker of the poor.
A person feels joy when others suffer disaster.
This person will not escape punishment.
passages.original: לֹעֵ֣ג לָ֭רָשׁ חֵרֵ֣ף עֹשֵׂ֑הוּ שָׂמֵ֥חַ לְ֝אֵ֗יד לֹ֣א יִנָּקֶֽה׃

passages.text: Grandchildren are the crown of the aged, and the glory of a son is his father.
passages.sermon:
Old people have grandchildren.
Grandchildren are like a crown for old people.
A son has a father.
A father is the glory of his son.
passages.original: עֲטֶ֣רֶת זְ֭קֵנִים בְּנֵ֣י בָנִ֑ים וְתִפְאֶ֖רֶת בָּנִ֣ים אֲבוֹתָֽם׃

passages.text: Eloquent words are unfit for a fool; how much worse are lying lips to a ruler!
passages.sermon:
A fool cannot use eloquent words well.
Eloquent words do not suit a fool.
A ruler must not speak lies.
Lying lips are even worse for a ruler.
passages.original: לֹא־ נָאוָ֣ה לְנָבָ֣ל שְׂפַת־ יֶ֑תֶר אַ֝֗ף כִּֽי־ לְנָדִ֥יב שְׂפַת־ שָֽׁקֶר׃

passages.text: A bribe is a charm to its giver; wherever he turns, he succeeds.
passages.sermon:
A bribe looks valuable to the person who gives it.
The giver sees the bribe as a charm.
Wherever the giver goes, he thinks the bribe will help him succeed.
He believes the bribe brings him success in every situation.
passages.original: אֶֽבֶן־ חֵ֣ן הַ֭שֹּׁחַד בְּעֵינֵ֣י בְעָלָ֑יו אֶֽל־ כָּל־ אֲשֶׁ֖ר יִפְנֶ֣ה יַשְׂכִּֽיל׃

passages.text: Whoever conceals an offense promotes love, but he who brings it up separates friends.
passages.sermon: A person who hides another’s wrongdoing wants to show love.\r\nA person who repeats or brings up the matter causes friends to separate.
passages.original: מְֽכַסֶּה־ פֶּ֭שַׁע מְבַקֵּ֣שׁ אַהֲבָ֑ה וְשֹׁנֶ֥ה בְ֝דָבָ֗ר מַפְרִ֥יד אַלּֽוּף׃

passages.text: A rebuke cuts into a man of discernment deeper than a hundred lashes cut into a fool.
passages.sermon:
A man of discernment listens carefully.
He understands when someone rebukes him.
A rebuke affects him deeply.
A fool does not learn easily.
Even if someone strikes a fool a hundred times, he does not understand.
A single rebuke teaches a discerning man more than many blows teach a fool.
passages.original: תֵּ֣חַת גְּעָרָ֣ה בְמֵבִ֑ין מֵהַכּ֖וֹת כְּסִ֣יל מֵאָֽה׃

passages.text: An evil man seeks only rebellion; a cruel messenger will be sent against him.
passages.sermon:
An evil man always seeks rebellion.
He does not want peace.
God will send a cruel messenger against him.
This messenger will punish the evil man.
passages.original: אַךְ־ מְרִ֥י יְבַקֶּשׁ־ רָ֑ע וּמַלְאָ֥ךְ אַ֝כְזָרִ֗י יְשֻׁלַּח־ בּֽוֹ׃

passages.text: It is better to meet a bear robbed of her cubs than a fool in his folly.
passages.sermon:
A bear robbed of her cubs is very dangerous.
A man who meets such a bear faces great danger.
A fool acts with reckless foolishness.
A fool in his folly is even more dangerous than the bear.
It is better to meet the angry bear than to meet a fool acting in his foolishness.
passages.original: פָּג֬וֹשׁ דֹּ֣ב שַׁכּ֣וּל בְּאִ֑ישׁ וְאַל־ כְּ֝סִ֗יל בְּאִוַּלְתּֽוֹ׃

passages.text: If anyone returns evil for good, evil will never leave his house.
passages.sermon:
A person may receive good from someone.
This person may choose to return evil instead of good.
If a person returns evil for good, evil will stay with him.
Evil will never leave his house.
passages.original: מֵשִׁ֣יב רָ֭עָה תַּ֣חַת טוֹבָ֑ה לֹא־ תָמִישׁ רָ֝עָ֗ה מִבֵּיתֽוֹ׃

passages.text: To start a quarrel is to release a flood; so abandon the dispute before it breaks out.
passages.sermon:
A quarrel is like water breaking out.
When you start a quarrel, you release trouble like a flood.
Stop the argument before it begins.
Leave the dispute before it grows.
passages.original: פּ֣וֹטֵֽר מַ֭יִם רֵאשִׁ֣ית מָד֑וֹן וְלִפְנֵ֥י הִ֝תְגַּלַּ֗ע הָרִ֥יב נְטֽוֹשׁ׃

passages.text: Acquitting the guilty and condemning the righteous— both are detestable to the LORD.
passages.sermon:
The LORD hates certain actions.
He hates when someone says a guilty person is innocent.
He also hates when someone says an innocent person is guilty.
Both actions are detestable to the LORD.
passages.original: מַצְדִּ֣יק רָ֭שָׁע וּמַרְשִׁ֣יעַ צַדִּ֑יק תּוֹעֲבַ֥ת יְ֝הוָ֗ה גַּם־ שְׁנֵיהֶֽם׃

passages.text: Why should the fool have money in his hand with no intention of buying wisdom?
passages.sermon:
A fool is a person who lacks understanding.
A fool may have money in his hand.
He does not use his money to gain wisdom.
He has no desire to learn.
He does not seek understanding.
Money is useless to him for gaining wisdom.
passages.original: לָמָּה־ זֶּ֣ה מְחִ֣יר בְּיַד־ כְּסִ֑יל לִקְנ֖וֹת חָכְמָ֣ה וְלֶב־ אָֽיִן׃

passages.text: A friend loves at all times, and a brother is born for adversity.
passages.sermon:
A true friend always loves.
A friend shows love in every situation.
A brother is born to help in times of trouble.
A brother stands with you during hardship.
passages.original: בְּכָל־ עֵ֭ת אֹהֵ֣ב הָרֵ֑עַ וְאָ֥ח לְ֝צָרָ֗ה יִוָּלֵֽד׃

passages.text: A man lacking judgment strikes hands in pledge and puts up security for his neighbor.
passages.sermon:
A man without good judgment acts foolishly.
He makes a promise by shaking hands.
He agrees to be responsible for his neighbor’s debt.
He puts up security for his neighbor.
He does this in front of others.
passages.original: אָדָ֣ם חֲסַר־ לֵ֭ב תּוֹקֵ֣עַ כָּ֑ף עֹרֵ֥ב עֲ֝רֻבָּ֗ה לִפְנֵ֥י רֵעֵֽהוּ׃

passages.text: He who loves transgression loves strife; he who builds his gate high invites destruction.
passages.sermon:
A person who loves to do wrong also loves conflict.
A person who makes his gate high seeks his own ruin.
A person who desires sin desires arguments.
A person who exalts himself brings trouble on himself.
passages.original: אֹ֣הֵֽב פֶּ֭שַׁע אֹהֵ֣ב מַצָּ֑ה מַגְבִּ֥יהַּ פִּ֝תְח֗וֹ מְבַקֶּשׁ־ שָֽׁבֶר׃

passages.text: The one with a perverse heart finds no good, and he whose tongue is deceitful falls into trouble.
passages.sermon:
A person with a perverse heart does not find good.
A perverse heart means a heart that twists what is right.
A person who speaks with a deceitful tongue falls into trouble.
A deceitful tongue means a person who lies or misleads others.
Trouble comes to those who use their words to deceive.
passages.original: עִקֶּשׁ־ לֵ֭ב לֹ֣א יִמְצָא־ ט֑וֹב וְנֶהְפָּ֥ךְ בִּ֝לְשׁוֹנ֗וֹ יִפּ֥וֹל בְּרָעָֽה׃

passages.text: A man fathers a fool to his own grief; the father of a fool has no joy.
passages.sermon: A man who has a foolish child feels sorrow.\r\nThe father of a fool does not feel joy.
passages.original: יֹלֵ֣ד כְּ֭סִיל לְת֣וּגָה ל֑וֹ וְלֹֽא־ יִ֝שְׂמַ֗ח אֲבִ֣י נָבָֽל׃

passages.text: A joyful heart is good medicine, but a broken spirit dries up the bones.
passages.sermon:
A joyful heart brings healing.
A joyful heart acts like good medicine.
A broken spirit causes harm.
A broken spirit dries up the bones.
passages.original: לֵ֣ב שָׂ֭מֵחַ יֵיטִ֣ב גֵּהָ֑ה וְר֥וּחַ נְ֝כֵאָ֗ה תְּיַבֶּשׁ־ גָּֽרֶם׃

passages.text: A wicked man takes a covert bribe to subvert the course of justice.
passages.sermon: A wicked man takes a bribe in secret.\r\nHe does this to change the path of justice.\r\nHe uses the bribe to make justice unfair.
passages.original: שֹׁ֣חַד מֵ֭חֵיק רָשָׁ֣ע יִקָּ֑ח לְ֝הַטּ֗וֹת אָרְח֥וֹת מִשְׁפָּֽט׃

passages.text: Wisdom is the focus of the discerning, but the eyes of a fool wander to the ends of the earth.
passages.sermon:
A discerning person focuses on wisdom.
A discerning person pays attention to what is wise.
A fool does not focus on wisdom.
A fool lets his eyes wander everywhere.
A fool looks to the ends of the earth.
A fool does not keep his attention on what matters.
passages.original: אֶת־ פְּנֵ֣י מֵבִ֣ין חָכְמָ֑ה וְעֵינֵ֥י כְ֝סִ֗יל בִּקְצֵה־ אָֽרֶץ׃

passages.text: A foolish son brings grief to his father and bitterness to her who bore him.
passages.sermon: A foolish son causes grief to his father.\r\nA foolish son brings bitterness to his mother.
passages.original: כַּ֣עַס לְ֭אָבִיו בֵּ֣ן כְּסִ֑יל וּ֝מֶ֗מֶר לְיוֹלַדְתּֽוֹ׃

passages.text: It is surely not good to punish the innocent or to flog a noble for his honesty.
passages.sermon:
This verse teaches about justice and fairness.
A righteous person does what is right.
It is not good to punish a righteous person.
A noble person acts with honesty.
It is not good to strike a noble person for being honest.
passages.original: גַּ֤ם עֲנ֣וֹשׁ לַצַּדִּ֣יק לֹא־ ט֑וֹב לְהַכּ֖וֹת נְדִיבִ֣ים עַל־ יֹֽשֶׁר׃

passages.text: A man of knowledge restrains his words, and a man of understanding maintains a calm spirit.
passages.sermon:
A man of knowledge does not speak many words.
He restrains his speech.
A man of understanding stays calm.
He keeps a cool spirit.
passages.original: חוֹשֵׂ֣ךְ אֲ֭מָרָיו יוֹדֵ֣עַ דָּ֑עַת וְקַר ר֝֗וּחַ אִ֣ישׁ תְּבוּנָֽה׃

passages.text: Even a fool is considered wise if he keeps silent, and discerning when he holds his tongue.
passages.sermon: A fool is a person who lacks wisdom.\r\nPeople consider a fool wise if he stays silent.\r\nPeople see him as discerning if he keeps his mouth shut.
passages.original: גַּ֤ם אֱוִ֣יל מַ֭חֲרִישׁ חָכָ֣ם יֵחָשֵׁ֑ב אֹטֵ֖ם שְׂפָתָ֣יו נָבֽוֹן׃
